findings.subject: menu
findings.summary: The shared menu recipe has no forced-colors handling: a highlighted (keyboard-focused) row is shown only by background-color and every row sets outline:none, so in Windows High Contrast the focused item of DropdownMenu, ContextMenu, Menubar (and Command rows, which copy the pattern) is invisible.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/menu/menu.css:79 (outline:none on .a63-Menu-item), :96-101 (highlight = background-color/background-image/box-shadow only); packages/ui-react/src/components/command/command.css:193-199 (same for .a63-Command-item); grep -rln forced-colors packages/styles/src packages/ui-react/src -> only button/button.css. Base UI moves DOM focus onto the item, so no outline means no focus indicator once forced colors strip backgrounds and shadows.
findings.fix: Add @media (forced-colors: active) to menu.css and command.css: .a63-Menu-item[data-highlighted], .a63-Command-item[data-highlighted] { outline: 2px solid Highlight; outline-offset: -2px } (or background: Highlight; color: HighlightText; forced-color-adjust: none). Add a forced-colors emulation baseline for the Menu Preview story.

verified.reason: Checked it in the source. menu.css:79 sets outline:none on .a63-Menu-item, and the [data-highlighted] rule (menu.css:96-101) uses only background-color, background-image and box-shadow. command.css:193-199 does the same for .a63-Command-item. The only component CSS with a forced-colors rule is button/button.css; the other hits are changelogs, docs and audit files. With forced colors on, backgrounds become the system Canvas colour, shadows are dropped and outline stays none, so the focused row has no visible indicator. The bar lists forced colors under K2, so P1 holds.

findings.subject: menu
findings.summary: Menu group labels fail text contrast: the recipe draws them in text-secondary at opacity 0.75 at the xs size, measured 3.36:1 on the modern light popup (WCAG 1.4.3 needs 4.5:1 for this size). Every Dropdown/Context/Menubar/Select label inherits it.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/menu/menu.css:179-188 (.a63-Menu-label: color text-secondary, font-size control-font-size-xs, opacity:0.75). Measured on apps/storybook/visual/__screenshots__/ui-react-menu-themes-chromium-linux.png: 'ACTIONS' label darkest pixel (138,138,138) on popup (252,252,252) = 3.36:1; same baseline aqua/dark label 3.19:1. Shortcut text without the opacity measures 5.77:1, so the opacity is the cause.
findings.fix: Remove opacity:0.75 from .a63-Menu-label (rely on text-secondary, which passes), and add the label/popup pair to the declared contrast pairs so the role check covers it.

verified.reason: Reproduced from the tokens, not only the screenshot. The label uses --a63-text-secondary, which resolves to surface-light-11 = rgba(100,100,100). With opacity 0.75 over a popup of about 252, that gives 0.75*100 + 0.25*252 = 138, i.e. (138,138,138). Contrast against 252 computes to 3.36:1. The label is 12-13px at weight 600, below the large-text size, so WCAG 1.4.3 asks for 4.5:1. Select, Command and Autocomplete labels reuse the same colour token. The opacity is set in menu.css, so it applies at least to the menu-based labels.

findings.subject: menu
findings.summary: The menu contract lists tones neutral|primary, but no component exposes a tone prop; the primary highlight is reachable only by passing an undocumented raw data-tone attribute on the popup.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-foundation/contracts/components/menu.json lists tones ['neutral','primary']; packages/ui-react/src/components/menu/menu.css:105-112 keys on .a63-Menu-popup[data-tone='primary']; grep 'tone' in dropdown-menu.tsx, context-menu.tsx, menubar.tsx -> no matches; only menu.stories.tsx sets data-tone.
findings.fix: Add tone?: 'neutral' | 'primary' (default from menuContract.defaultTone) to DropdownMenuContent, ContextMenuContent, MenubarContent and their SubContent parts, stamped as data-tone; document it in the dropdown-menu page.

findings.subject: menu

findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/menu/menu.css:59-62 min-height: max(control-height-sm*density, --a63-control-min-size); packages/styles/src/contracts/environment.css:69-77 defines --a63-row-min-size for exactly this case and :128-137 sets it to 2.75rem under pointer:coarse while control-min-size is 2rem.

findings.subject: context-menu
findings.summary: ContextMenuContent and ContextMenuSubContent ignore PortalContainerProvider and offer no portalContainer prop, unlike DropdownMenu, so inside a scoped provider or shadow root the context menu portals to body and loses the scope.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/context-menu/context-menu.tsx:97-121 (Portal with only portalProps); compare dropdown-menu.tsx:111-112 (usePortalContainer fallback). grep usePortalContainer -> dropdown-menu, hover-card, popover, preview-card, select, sheet, toaster, tooltip; not context-menu, not navigation-menu.
findings.fix: Read usePortalContainer() and add portalContainer to ContextMenuContentProps/SubContentProps, as DropdownMenu does; add the same test as dropdown-menu.test.tsx 'portals submenu content into the requested container'.

findings.subject: navigation-menu

findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/navigation-menu/navigation-menu.tsx NavigationMenuIndicator renders <div className='a63-NavigationMenu-indicator'> with no primitive; navigation-menu.css:251-256 depends on data-state; navigation-menu.test.tsx has no indicator test.
findings.fix: Wire it to a Base UI part (e.g. NavigationMenu.Arrow inside the popup) or remove the export with a changeset.

findings.subject: navigation-menu

findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/navigation-menu/navigation-menu.tsx NavigationMenuPositioner: <Portal container={portalContainer}> with no usePortalContainer().
findings.fix: Use portalContainer ?? usePortalContainer().

findings.subject: navigation-menu
findings.summary: Open trigger and active link are marked by background only (surface-muted), so in forced-colors mode the current section and the open trigger are indistinguishable.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/navigation-menu/navigation-menu.css:78-81 and :223-226 (background only for [data-popup-open] and [data-active]); no forced-colors rule.
findings.fix: Add a forced-colors rule (outline or border in Highlight) for [data-popup-open] and [data-active].

findings.subject: tabs
findings.summary: The selected tab in the default and underline variants is shown only by the indicator's background (a plate or a 2px bar) plus a text-color change, so in forced-colors mode the selected tab cannot be told from the others.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/tabs/tabs.css:268-287 (indicator = background + box-shadow); selected text only swaps text-secondary -> text-primary (tabs.css:139 and active rule), which forced colors flattens to CanvasText; grep forced-colors tabs.css -> 0.
findings.fix: Add @media (forced-colors: active) { .a63-Tabs-indicator { background: Highlight; forced-color-adjust: none } } (or a border/underline on [data-active] in Highlight), and a forced-colors baseline for the Variants story.

verified.reason: In tabs.css the default variant marks the selected tab with a surface-overlay background plus control-shadow. The underline variant uses a 2px background bar (action-primary). The selected tab itself only changes colour from text-secondary to text-primary (tabs.css:190-192 and :227-229). tabs.css has no forced-colors rule. With forced colors on, the plate and bar backgrounds become Canvas, the shadow is dropped and both text colours become CanvasText, so nothing marks the selected tab in these two variants. The attached variant has a border-color plus font-weight 600 and is not covered by this claim.

findings.subject: tabs

findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/tabs/tabs.css:133 min-width: var(--a63-control-min-target) but :134 height: var(--tabs-height, 2.25rem) with no min-target floor; the default variant ::after only extends by --tabs-inset (tabs.css:155-160).
findings.fix: Extend the hit area on coarse pointers (block-axis ::after sized to --a63-control-min-target), keeping the rendered ramp.

findings.subject: command
findings.summary: Command's own behaviour is untested: three render-only tests, no test that typing filters items, that arrow keys and Enter pick an item, that the empty state appears, or that the dialog opens and closes; no APG binding exists for it, and the pattern registry has no editable combobox pattern.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/command/command.test.tsx:54-90 ('renders the search input', 'renders the items from the items prop', 'replaces the input icon...'); no userEvent/fireEvent in the file; apps/storybook/a11y/patterns.test.ts:56-102 binds dialog, alert-dialog, dropdown-menu, tabs, select, switch, checkbox, accordion, radio only; packages/ui-foundation/src/a11y/index.ts:46-56 has no list-autocomplete combobox. Command forces inline/open/autoHighlight/keepHighlight (command.tsx Command), which nothing verifies.
findings.fix: Add behaviour tests: type a query -> non-matching items removed and CommandEmpty shown; ArrowDown/Enter fires onValueChange/the item action; Escape closes CommandDialog and returns focus to the trigger. Add a combobox-list pattern contract and bind the Inline story.

verified.reason: command.test.tsx has exactly three tests (lines 54, 61, 68), all render-only, and none uses userEvent, fireEvent or the keyboard. No other test file references Command. apps/storybook/a11y/patterns.test.ts imports only the accordion, alert-dialog, checkbox, dialog, dropdown-menu, radio, select, switch and tabs stories. ui-foundation a11yPatterns has only 'combobox-select-only', with no autocomplete or list combobox pattern. command.tsx forces inline, open, autoHighlight='always' and keepHighlight, and nothing checks those. Filtering itself comes from Base UI Autocomplete, which lowers the risk a little, but the wrapper's own behaviour and the dialog open/close are untested. Under K9 ('Untested behaviour') P1 holds.

findings.subject: command

findings.subject: command
findings.summary: The command dialog viewport ignores safe areas and has no phone story; it is position:fixed inset 0 with plain padding and opens the keyboard immediately (autoFocus).
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/command/command.css:25-38 (.a63-Command-viewport padding max(1rem,4vh) var(--a63-space-4), no --a63-safe-area-*); compare navigation-menu.css:161-164 which subtracts safe areas; grep phone/mobile in command.stories.tsx -> 0.
findings.fix: Add the safe-area insets to the viewport padding and a phone-width Dialog story with the popup open.

findings.subject: command
findings.summary: Empty and disabled states are in the contract but not captured: no story shows CommandEmpty with a query, or a disabled item.
findings.evidence: command.json states ['closed','open','empty','highlighted','disabled','focus-visible']; grep disabled command.stories.tsx -> 0; apps/storybook/visual/__screenshots__/ui-react-command-dialog-chromium-linux.png is 10.5 KB (closed trigger).
findings.fix: Add an Empty story (defaultValue query with no match), a disabled item, and an open Dialog baseline.

findings.subject: menubar
findings.summary: Menubar triggers have no height floor or touch-target expansion; at 4px block padding they render about 23-28px tall on every pointer.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/menubar/menubar.css:36-53 (.a63-Menubar-trigger padding space-1 x space-2, no min-height, no ::before target); only the bar has a min-height (:18-21).
findings.fix: Floor the trigger at the control ramp and expand to --a63-control-min-target on coarse pointers, as button.css does.

findings.subject: menubar
findings.summary: Menubar's defining behaviour (Left/Right between menus, opening the next menu while one is open) is untested and has no APG binding; the a11y registry has no menubar pattern.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/menubar/menubar.test.tsx (3 render tests, no key events); packages/ui-foundation/src/a11y/index.ts:46-56 (no menubar); patterns.test.ts:56-102.
findings.fix: Add a menubar pattern contract (APG Menubar) and bind the Playground story; add a keyboard test.

findings.subject: menubar
findings.summary: Menubar and DropdownMenu drift in small ways: MenubarCheckboxItem/RadioItem take inset but DropdownMenuCheckboxItem/RadioItem do not; menubar uses lucide Check while dropdown/context draw an inline CheckIcon; the recipe comment still names a63-DropdownMenu-* classes.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/menubar/menubar.tsx:126-180 vs dropdown-menu.tsx:158-200; menubar.css:7 'inherited from the DropdownMenu recipe (a63-DropdownMenu-*)' while the classes are a63-Menu-*.
findings.fix: Give the dropdown/context checkable items inset, use one indicator glyph source, fix the comment.

findings.subject: context-menu
findings.summary: ContextMenu has render-only tests and no APG binding; right-click open, long-press on touch, keyboard navigation and dismissal are untested.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/context-menu/context-menu.test.tsx (3 tests: trigger slot, open popup parts, item variant; no key/pointer events); contextMenuContract has no accessibility binding (contract JSON has no 'accessibility').
findings.fix: Bind the menu pattern (opener: contextmenu event) to the Playground story and add a long-press/keyboard test.

findings.subject: navigation-menu
findings.summary: NavigationMenu has render-only tests; opening on hover/click, Escape, and keyboard movement between triggers and into the panel are untested and unbound to any APG pattern.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/navigation-menu/navigation-menu.test.tsx (3 tests: slots, expanded content links, trigger style helper).
findings.fix: Add a disclosure-navigation pattern binding or keyboard tests for trigger -> panel -> Escape.

findings.subject: pagination
findings.summary: Previous/Next chevrons are not mirrored, so in dir=rtl 'Previous' points forward.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/pagination/pagination.tsx:85 ChevronLeft, :102 ChevronRight; pagination.css has no rtl rule (grep rtl -> none).
findings.fix: Add :where([dir='rtl']) .a63-Pagination-nav-link svg { transform: scaleX(-1) } as breadcrumb.css:66-68 does.

findings.subject: pagination
findings.summary: There is no disabled state for Previous/Next at the first and last page: the contract lists only rest and current, the parts have no disabled prop, and the Button render path puts type="button" and a disabled attribute that anchors ignore.
findings.evidence: pagination.json states ['rest','current']; pagination.tsx:52-69 PaginationLink renders Button with render={<a>}; packages/ui-react/src/components/button/button.tsx:103-104 always sets disabled and type ?? 'button' (also reported in readiness/k01-actions.json for button).
findings.fix: Add a disabled prop that sets aria-disabled='true', drops href and styles data-disabled; add 'disabled' to the contract states and a story.

findings.subject: pagination
findings.summary: The landmark labels are hard-coded lowercase English ('pagination', 'breadcrumb'); the screen reader announces 'pagination navigation' and there is no documented way to localize except overriding aria-label.
findings.evidence: pagination.tsx:18 aria-label='pagination'; breadcrumb.tsx Breadcrumb aria-label='breadcrumb'; pagination.tsx:80,96 English aria-labels.
findings.fix: Capitalize ('Pagination', 'Breadcrumb') and document aria-label overrides for localization in the docs page.

findings.subject: breadcrumb
findings.summary: No long-segment handling: segments wrap and break mid-word, with no truncation option and no long, CJK or RTL story.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/breadcrumb/breadcrumb.css:8-21 (flex-wrap: wrap; word-break: break-word); breadcrumb.stories.tsx exports Playground, Collapsed, CustomSeparator, Themes, Endpoints, ContractMetadata only.
findings.fix: Add a LongTrail story (long English, CJK, dir=rtl) and decide whether middle segments truncate with an ellipsis.

findings.subject: breadcrumb
findings.summary: BreadcrumbLink still carries the deprecated asChild boolean beside render.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/breadcrumb/breadcrumb.tsx BreadcrumbLinkProps '/** @deprecated Use render instead */ asChild?: boolean'.
findings.fix: Schedule removal in the next major.

findings.subject: context-menu, menubar, command, navigation-menu, breadcrumb, pagination
findings.summary: Six of the nine subjects have only the generated catalog page: the CLI answer is an import line, one specific guidance line plus two boilerplate lines repeated verbatim across all six, and no runnable example; only dropdown-menu and tabs have a written docs page.
findings.evidence: `pnpm -s atom63 component context-menu|menubar|command|navigation-menu|breadcrumb|pagination` each print 'Preserve link, menu, command, or selection semantics instead of styling generic containers.' and 'Expose current location when applicable and verify alternate input paths at narrow widths.' and a bare import; apps/docs/src/pages has component-dropdown-menu.mdx and component-tabs.mdx only. `atom63 example context-menu` does return a story file.
findings.fix: Write docs pages (or contract-driven sections) with a runnable snippet and real guidance per component: command (labels, dialog name, filtering), menubar (desktop-only use), navigation-menu (links vs triggers), breadcrumb (collapse), pagination (disabled ends, URLs).

findings.subject: dropdown-menu
findings.summary: The iOS Menu snapshot shows only the closed trigger, and its tint is the system blue rather than a visible theme accent.
findings.evidence: examples/ios-demo/Atom63DemoTests/__Snapshots__/iPhone-17-Pro_iOS-26.2/menu.light.png (viewed: 'Project actions' trigger + 'No action selected').
findings.fix: Accept as platform-adaptive (native Menu cannot be snapshotted open) or add a snapshot of the menu content as a list.

findings.subject: context-menu
findings.summary: ContextMenu declares no iOS renderer although SwiftUI has a native .contextMenu modifier.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-foundation/contracts/components/context-menu.json has no crossRenderer block (atom63 component context-menu shows no iOS section).
findings.fix: Add crossRenderer with swiftUIRenderer '.contextMenu' and parity platform-adaptive.
